Haunting bird call carries over the still gray water, reflecting the overcast sky above. A soft splash echoes, followed by another from the gentle rhythm of a 
paddling canoe. The Traveler rolls their shoulders, still tired from the upriver struggle, but now finally settling into the peace of the lake that opens wide 
before them, hemmed in by a standing thicket of trees that thickly encroach upon the shore.
 
Breathing a sigh of relief, they pull in the oar and settle into the canoe, getting their journal from the knapsack that they used as back support and begin 
to sketch their recent findings. The Fenlands, while as dangerous as any other inch of this primal land, hosts creatures unsure of what to make of the 
curious wooden object that floats above them so, in a rare moment, the Traveler relaxes.
 
Nearly nodding off in the warm afternoon, a bump shakes them awake. Gripping their journal to their chest and slowly peering over the edge, a long train 
of mottled, rubbery flesh rises in a sequence of rounded peaks, leaving no ripple in their wake. Each undulation bumping the canoe as the monstrously 
huge aquatic creature traverses its watery domain, unconcerned by what it must think is only drift wood as it hunts for a larger meal. Not wanting to 
dispel the creature of its misunderstanding, the Traveler quietly settles back into the canoe and patiently waits before attempting to row once more to the 
distant, and hopefully safer huddle of trees near the lake shore.
The Fenlands favor adaptability, and few creatures exemplify that more than amphibians, so it is of little surprise that one such as that 
grew to be the largest and most dominating creature in this watery ecosystem. The nuthorghull flourishes only because most other 
creatures would otherwise be limited by the confines of their environment. While best suited for an aquatic existence, this incredibly 
long tailed salamander can pull itself out onto the muddy banks to seek terrestrial prey or, just simply, find fresher more abundant 
bodies of water. While much larger, it fills the niche once held by crocodiles, able to hunt through the murk with the use of its catfish-
like barbels, tasting the presence of nearby prey. These tactile, extrasensory organs allow the amphibian to sift through the cold mud 
and focus in on the trail of scents that lead to live prey, eschewing the need for vision within these dark and obscure depths. When 
winter approaches and the lakes become cold and stagnant, the salamanders will settle into the mud to hibernate, their long sinuous 
tails storing rich fats to endure long unmoving seasons. Unlike many species, the nuthorghull will breed in the late seasons and spend 
their wintering hibernation clutching their spawn of eggs. Nestled in clutches, both males and females protect their future offspring 
from the frigid water and any hungry ovivores that may want to stifle the next generation.
The appetites of apex predators have a massive influence on their surrounding ecosystem; even in their absence, the impact 
is noticeable. While many of the Fenlands megafauna may not always feel the hunger of a nuthorghull in their environment, 
after millions of years of island isolation, they have all adapted to be wary of the great amphibian that looms in the mud and silt. 
Only swimming in the deepest of lakes and widest of rivers, the nuthorghull does not claim large swaths of territory for itself like 
many other apex predators, and it instead grows to fit the competition it lives within, and when surrounded by many of their own 
species, will grow to less monumental sizes. Though Rootwell may be home to the largest of their kind, the isolation of the single 
lake leaves them little space to breed and it may not be long before they disappear from that black, forested lake. Some of their young 
attempt to breach into the many rivers that feed the large central lake, but can only go so far before the rivers narrow into rapids. 
Further east, shallow Four Moon has managed to create a kind of community of nuthorghull that settle in the mud, reaching out to the 
three smaller satellite lakes to feast and leave the larger middle lake to spawn and hibernate. To the north west, the mountain's frigid 
waters of the Inmere lake leave the amphibians more sluggish than their southern kin. Though their movements are more languid, 
they feast and breed with ease as the brackish Astradale bay and the Rhaen river feeds them untold numbers of migrating prey. 
Even with their vast appetite, they are merely a hurdle to overcome for many of the fish that run these waters each breeding season. 
 
As the nuthorghull are unrivaled in size, many of the Fenlands' other predators are found to be more stealthy than aggressive, as they 
could never hope to contend with the massive amphibian in being the environment's dominating species. Larkiera and murrow use 
the dour tones of their body to hide among the grass and mud, silvette keep to the surface and hope to pass quickly unseen in the river 
Rhaen. While the rest remain near the water, quick to rush away from the edge the moment the great beasts rears its wide head. Many 
herbivores and grazers, who would otherwise clear the lake bottom of sea weed are then left absent, leading to massive flourishing 
growths that enrich the surrounding forests and rivers downstream. Left unchecked, this often leads to algae blooms that cover vast 
stretches of the lakes in a thick, green, choking carpet.
 
Fortunately for many, the environments in which the nuthorghull dwell within keep it mostly contained to those vast and deep waters, 
as it can be quite slow and lumbering to carry its weight outside the water. For those brave enough to dive into the black depths, there 
is little they can do to ward off the beast. Lying in thick layers of mud along the bottom, most of its massive form rests unseen. Once 
it begins to move, only the stirring clouds of silt warns of its approach. Algae-choked waters leave little light to illuminate its domain 
and any submerged creature, be it fish or Traveler, have little hope to escape its gaping maw once their questing barbels have tasted 
and awakened its unending hunger.
